question.problem:
Calculate $∇\cdot (-4F)$ for the vector field $F$ where

$$
F={x}^{2}yz\,i+({y}^{3}-y)\,j-xy{z}^{2}\,k.
$$
question.worked_solution:
If $F$ and $G$ are vector fields and $k$ is a constant, then we have the following  linearity properties for divergence:

- $∇\cdot (kF)=k∇\cdot F$

- $∇\cdot (F+G)=∇\cdot F+∇\cdot G.$

In our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\cdot (-4F)=-4∇\cdot F.\end{aligned}
$$

First, we need to calculate $∇\cdot F.$ In doing so, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\cdot F & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}yz)+\frac{∂}{∂y}({y}^{3}-y)+\frac{∂}{∂z}(-xy{z}^{2}) \\  & =2xyz+3{y}^{2}-1-2xyz \\  & =3{y}^{2}-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the linearity properties, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\cdot (-4F) & =-4∇\cdot F \\  & =-4\cdot (3{y}^{2}-1) \\  & =4-12{y}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
